title: Pressure washer: safe teardown
summary: A pressure washer gives a horizontal-shaft petrol engine or a mains motor, a small high-pressure pump, a rated hose, gun and nozzles, and a wheeled frame. Before you undo any hose, stop the engine or unplug the motor, turn the water off and squeeze the trigger until the pressure is gone: the jet can force water under your skin.

steps.text: Shut it down in this order, outdoors on level ground: release the trigger; stop the engine, or switch the motor off and pull the plug; close the engine's fuel valve if it has one; turn off the water supply. Then point the gun at the ground, away from people, and squeeze the trigger until the water stops (Simpson MSH3125 manual, Predator 62214 manual, Sun Joe SPX3000 manual).
steps.warn: The jet can cut skin and force water under it. Never undo a hose or fitting while it holds pressure, and never cover a leak with your hand. An injection wound is not a simple cut: get it treated at once (Simpson MSH3125 manual).

steps.text: Electric models: keep the plug out from here on and keep it where you can see it. Sun Joe says to pull the plug before servicing, cleaning or removing any part (Sun Joe SPX3000 manual).
steps.warn: A washer with an automatic stop can sit silent with its switch on: the Sun Joe turns its motor off by itself when the water stops (Sun Joe SPX3000 manual). Unplug before you squeeze the trigger or touch anything.

steps.text: Petrol models: let the engine, muffler and pump cool, then pull the cap off the spark plug and tuck it away from the plug (Predator 62214 manual, Simpson MSH3125 manual).

Undo the garden hose from the pump inlet, then the high-pressure hose from the pump and from the gun. Take the wand out of the gun and lock the trigger. Drain the water out of the hoses, gun and pump (Predator 62214 manual).
Petrol models: pump the fuel out of the tank into a fuel can with a hand pump, with the fuel valve closed, outdoors and away from flames (safety_fuel_handling).
steps.warn: Never start a siphon by mouth. Don't run the engine to empty the tank: without water flowing the pump overheats, and Predator warns an idling pump can expel very hot water (Predator 62214 manual).

steps.text: Petrol models: drain the engine oil. Stand the engine level, put a pan under the crankcase drain plug and take the plug out. If it will not drain, tip the engine only slightly, with the carburettor on the high side: the carburettor bowl can still hold petrol after the tank is empty (Predator 62214 manual). On the Simpson the drain plug is at the rear (Simpson MSH3125 manual). Seal and label the old oil.

Petrol models: take the pump off the engine. Put a block of wood under the pump to carry its weight. Undo the inlet fitting and filter and the outlet fitting, loosen the set screw on the shaft coupling if there is one, then undo the bolts that hold the pump to the engine (four on the Mi-T-M) and slide the pump off the crankshaft. Keep the shaft key (iFixit Mi-T-M pump).
steps.warn: Pumps can hold oil (the Simpson's is filled at the factory): keep the pump upright as it comes off, and don't tip the engine on its side while oil is still in it.

steps.text: Petrol models: undo the engine's mounting bolts and lift it off the frame. The engine is heavy: have a helper take its weight before the last bolt comes out. The Predator's parts list shows four engine mounting bolts (Predator 62214 manual). Keep the engine upright: Simpson warns that oil can fill the cylinder if it is stored on its side (Simpson MSH3125 manual).

Electric models: wait 5 minutes after unplugging, then open the motor's wiring cover without touching the terminals or any capacitor. Check your meter on a known live source, then measure at the motor's supply terminals and across any capacitor you find. Discharge any capacitor with a resistor tool (safety_discharge_capacitor) until it reads under 1 V, and leave a wire across its terminals. Check the meter on the live source again (safety_mains_isolation).
steps.warn: If the meter didn't read the live source before and after, its zero proved nothing. Never work on it plugged in.

steps.text: Electric models: unbolt the motor and pump from the frame and lift them out together, cutting the cable ties on the cord (iFixit Mi-T-M motor). Then stand the motor upright with the pump on top, undo the long bolts that clamp the pump to it, a little at a time in a cross pattern (four on the Kärcher) and lift the pump off (iFixit Kärcher pump).
steps.warn: On the Kärcher the motor housing holds the pump's oil. Keep it upright and pour the oil into a jar if you want to keep it (iFixit Kärcher pump).

steps.text: Keep the high-pressure hose, gun, wand and nozzles together as one kit. Take the detergent tank with its tube, the garden-hose inlet fitting and its filter screen, and on electric models the cord with its GFCI unit, freed by undoing its wires at the terminals you proved dead in step 9 (Predator 62214 manual, Sun Joe SPX3000 manual).
Take the wheels, axles, handle and frame (Predator 62214 manual). Leave the unloader and the thermal relief valve on the pump.

Store the pump drained and where it can't freeze: frost damage to the pump is permanent (Simpson MSH3125 manual, Sun Joe SPX3000 manual). Or run RV antifreeze through it (Simpson MSH3125 manual, Predator 62214 manual), and flush it all out with clear water before the pump is used again (Sun Joe SPX3000 manual). Store the engine upright.

notes:
## What's worth keeping and why

- **Engine (petrol models).** A horizontal-shaft four-stroke: the Predator 62214 has a 212 cc single-cylinder OHV engine (Predator 62214 manual). The pump slides onto a keyed crankshaft (iFixit Mi-T-M pump), so the bare shaft may take a pulley or coupling. Measure the shaft and its key before you plan a use for it. Run it only outdoors (safety_carbon_monoxide).
- **Pump.** A small high-pressure pump. The Predator's is an axial, direct-drive pump rated 3,100 psi (about 214 bar) at 2.8 US gal/min (about 10.6 L/min); its parts list shows three pistons, six check valves, a bypass jet, a detergent injector and an inlet filter (Predator 62214 manual). It sprays hard but moves little water. It needs water fed to it: Simpson asks for at least 20 psi and 5 gal/min at the inlet (Simpson MSH3125 manual). Uses: washing out tanks, drums and equipment, and spraying, wherever you can feed it from a tank or hose. Simpson warns to protect against backflow on a drinking-water supply, and Sun Joe says its washer must not be connected to the drinking-water mains (Simpson MSH3125 manual, Sun Joe SPX3000 manual).
- **Unloader and thermal relief valve.** When you release the trigger the pump goes into bypass and recirculates water. Simpson says not to leave it in bypass for more than 2 minutes, and its thermal relief valve dumps a gush of water when the pump gets too hot (Simpson MSH3125 manual). Predator warns the pump will expel very hot water if left idling (Predator 62214 manual). They stay on the pump.
- **Hose, gun, wand and nozzles.** The Predator has a 25 ft (7.6 m) pressure hose, a 21 in wand and five nozzles: 0°, 15°, 25°, 40° and soap (Predator 62214 manual). Use them only at or below the rating marked on them: Simpson says every accessory must be rated at least as high as the washer (Simpson MSH3125 manual).
- **Electric motor.** The Sun Joe SPX3000 draws 14.5 A on 120 V. It has a thermal sensor that protects the motor against overload, and a flow micro-switch that turns the motor off when the trigger is released (Sun Joe SPX3000 manual). Kärcher's K 5 Comfort Premium uses a water-cooled motor with a rated input power of 2.1 kW, which Kärcher contrasts with universal motors (Kärcher K 5 Comfort Premium). As a bench motor, run it through an RCD or GFCI with the terminals covered and keep clear of anything it spins (test_motor). Don't make its thermal sensor the only protection once it is out of the washer: a continuity reading doesn't prove it will still trip, so fit a fuse or breaker sized for the motor. Never heat the sensor to test it and never bridge it.
- **GFCI cord.** The Sun Joe's 35 ft (10.7 m) cord has a GFCI built in (Sun Joe SPX3000 manual). Keep it whole.
- **Wheels, axles and frame.** The Predator has two wheels on two axles, a frame and a handle (Predator 62214 manual): a start on a hand cart (build_hand_cart).
- **Fuel and oil.** Judge old fuel as in safety_fuel_handling.

## Variations

- **Predator 62214 (petrol):** 3,100 psi, 2.8 gal/min, axial direct-drive pump, 212 cc engine with a fuel valve, detergent tank (Predator 62214 manual).
- **Simpson MSH3125 (petrol):** 3,100 psi, 2.5 gal/min. The pump comes filled with oil and is sold as maintenance-free, with a thermal relief valve; the engine drain plug is at the rear (Simpson MSH3125 manual).
- **Mi-T-M CA2703HDHB1 (petrol):** four bolts and a keyed shaft with a 2.5 mm set screw hold the pump; later units have a tamper-proof unloader joined by pipe fittings (iFixit Mi-T-M pump).
- **Sun Joe SPX3000 (electric):** 120 V, 14.5 A, 2,030 psi maximum, 1.76 gal/min maximum, double insulated, GFCI cord (Sun Joe SPX3000 manual).
- **Mi-T-M CM1400HDEC1 (electric):** motor and pump come out as one assembly on four 11 mm bolts (iFixit Mi-T-M motor).
- **Kärcher 15209900 (electric):** the pump is clamped to the motor by four long bolts, and the motor housing is the pump's oil reservoir (iFixit Kärcher pump).
- Engine makes, bolt counts and whether a pump holds oil vary. Check yours as you go.

## What to leave

- **The unloader and thermal relief valve.** Don't strip or adjust them.
- **A pump that leaks oil.** Predator says not to run one (Predator 62214 manual).
- **A damaged hose.** Simpson says to replace a hose with cracks, bubbles, pinholes or melted spots (Simpson MSH3125 manual).
- **An opened electric washer, as a washer.** It is double insulated, with no earth, and Sun Joe leaves servicing to trained people (Sun Joe SPX3000 manual). Don't use it near water again unless every insulating part is back in place.

## Testing what you got out

- **Before you strip it:** connect water, take the nozzle off, point the wand where nobody is and hold the trigger for at least 30 seconds to purge the air, then start it and spray (Predator 62214 manual). Do it outdoors, never in a garage or shed (safety_carbon_monoxide), and never put a hand or foot in the jet. Never run it dry, and don't let it idle with the trigger up for more than 2 minutes: the pump can gush very hot water (Predator 62214 manual, Simpson MSH3125 manual). Run an electric model through a GFCI (Sun Joe SPX3000 manual).
- **Engine:** it ran in the test above, or check fuel, air filter and spark plug.
- **Motor:** test_motor, through an RCD or GFCI.
